Short facts relevant is, that the opposite party being plaintiff instituted the aforesaid Title Suit No. 226 of 1985 for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession on the averment that the suit plot along with other lands originally belonged to Budhu Majhi in rayati right and his name was correctly recorded in CS Khatian. Budhu Majhi sold the suit plot along with other lands to Haji Maran Ali Bepari by a registered kabala dated 13.3.43 and thereafter Haji Maran Ali Bepari sold away his purchased land, piece by piece, to different persons and the plaintiff opposite party purchased the suit plot measuring an area of 0.0932 acres of land by a registered kabala dated 24.3.64 and came into possession and had been possessing the same peacefully by mutating his name and paying all rents and taxes and that in the sale deed of the plaintiff the area of his purchased land was shown 0.08-1/4 acres but the boundary given in the schedule covered 0.0932 acres of land. The defendant had been illegally possessing a portion of the government acquired plot No. 936 to the contiguous west of the plaintiffs purchased land in plot No. 110 and that the defendant encroached the land of the plaintiff by the western portion of the suit land in middle of February, 1972 and constructed a semi-pucca building thereon. And further more on 20th September, 1981 the defendant constructed Sapra Ghar over the southern portion of the suit land and extended the semi pucca building in the east constructed earlier. The defendant also extended his boundary wall enclosing the plaintiffs land. 

 8. Mr. Md. Hannan, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff opposite party, submits that the learned trial Court did not commit any illegality in allowing amendment and that there is no bar for filing applications under Order 6 rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure at any stage for proper adjudication of a proceeding before the court and there is nothing to be aggrieved because the amendments quoted aforesaid are simply for clarification of certain facts for proper adjudication of the proceeding which in no way change the nature and character of the plaint or the suit itself. The last amendment for raising the quantum of land as 0.01125 in place of quantum amended earlier is simply in consonance with the earlier amendment. Mr. Hannan referred to the case of Shamsul Huque alias Ratan Mia Vs. Shaukat Ali alias Babul Bhuiyan and others reported in BCR 1985 (AD) 45 which was a suit for simple declaration of title without any consequential relief and during the pendency of the suit the defendant surreptitiously encroached upon a portion of land which was a ditch and thereafter the plaintiff proposed for amendment of the plaint with a prayer for recovery of khas possession for the encroached area and their Lordships have held by such amendment it will not change the nature and character of the suit and the amendment sought for will clearly describe the suit plot and their Lordships have further observed that the amendment sought at a preliminary stage before any evidence has been led. It appears from the record that written statement has already been filed and the defendant examined himself as DW 1 with the leave of the court in the year 1984 as he was going abroad for some time and was cross-examined and the case of the defendants was totally open for the plaintiff. The facts of the case are quite distinguishable and not applicable in this present case. The next case referred by the learned Advocate reported in 38 DLR 265 where it has been held that while considering an application for amendment of pleadings it is to be seen whether the amendment is necessary for the purpose of determining the real question of controversy in between the parties. But from the impugned order it appears that the learned trial Court allowed the amendment sought for as a matter of course without applying his judicial mind to that effect and such non-speaking orders are discarded always. I find no substance in the submissions advanced by the learned Advocate.
